text.bold: 2. The association doesn't show the direction.

paragraph.text: Meta-analyses from 2021 found an association between vegetarian diets and depressive symptoms, but most of the studies are cross-sectional, and the authors themselves point out that it's impossible to know whether the diet leads to depression or the reverse.

text.bold: 3. There are signs of reverse causation.

paragraph.text: A longitudinal German study found that many people began avoiding meat after a diagnosis of a mental disorder. Sensitivity to others' suffering may also be linked to both factors.
A lack of B12, iron or omega-3 can affect energy and mood, but it's prevented with supplementation and planning (G3, G4, G6).

People who perceive animal suffering and live with its normalization may feel isolation and distress. It's a hypothesis, still little studied, not a conclusion; but it shows that not every association with diet is nutritional.

The association between vegetarian diets and depressive symptoms appears in some studies and deserves serious investigation. Nutritional deficiencies can affect mood, and vegans should take care of them. It's also true that some vegans are in poor health, like people on any diet.
But a stereotype isn't evidence, and an association isn't a cause. With planning, a vegan diet supports healthy bodies and minds.
